Option 4: Continue current

2026-2027 for Wiltshire Creative, with the existing four core arts
and heritage organisations provides the most stable and
sustainable approach to delivery of the Council’s Priority 9
Make culture for everyone and avoids creating significant
inequalities or operational instability amongst the partner
organisations at this time.
 

Options considered

·        
Option 1: Cease funding to the arts and heritage
partners.

provision, undermine strategic Council objectives and impact the
sustainability of partner organisations.


·        
Option 2: Reduce funding allocations.

service delivery, community programmes and organisational
sustainability.


·        
Option 3: Redistribute funding based on revised
criteria.
This option was considered but rejected as it would create
significant uncertainty, potential reputational damage and unequal
impacts across organisations.

 

·        
Option 4: Continue current funding model through
Grant Agreements from 2026-2029, and 2026-2027 for Wiltshire
Creative, with the existing four core arts and heritage
organisations.

 

Continued funding at the current levels

Consultation with
Places Senior leadership team and relevant Wiltshire Council
officers.
 
Wiltshire Council
currently provides grant funding to six key arts and heritage
organisations through Partnership Agreements running from April
2023 to March 2026, Arts Council England research highlights the
positive impact of arts and culture on wellbeing, learning,
community cohesion and economic development, with the funded
organisations playing a significant role in providing these
benefits across Wiltshire.
 
Continued funding will
support the above organisations that deliver a wide range of
cultural activities, performances, exhibitions, learning programmes
and outreach work for residents, including children and young
people, vulnerable adults, disabled people, rural communities and
underrepresented groups.
 
New Grant Agreements
will align delivery with Wiltshire Council priorities and the
Wiltshire Cultural Strategy, focusing on increasing participation,
supporting children and young people, improving wellbeing,
enhancing place-shaping, promoting sustainability, driving
inclusive economic growth, developing skills and ensuring community
voices help shape cultural programmes. Performance is monitored
through six-monthly reports and annual reviews.
 
Funding approved
within the Council's 2026 budget.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Children’s Services, SEND, Education and Skills
purpose:
This report seeks approval to proceed with the
proposed enhanced end-to-end model for the Fostering South West
Hub, a regional collaborative arrangement involving local
authorities across the South West which Wiltshire Council jointly
leads with Cornwall Council. The enhanced model builds on the
existing regional marketing and single front door arrangements and
is intended to strengthen foster carer recruitment, assessment,
support and retention across the region. It responds to rising
demand for foster care, increasing complexity of children’s
needs and the need to improve local sufficiency, reduce delay and
support greater placement stability for children.
 
The Cabinet Member is asked to approve
progression of the enhanced Fostering South West Hub model on a
phased basis. Implementation activity will be progressed under
existing officer delegations and in accordance with the
Council’s Constitution, finance, procurement and legal
requirements. As the regional model develops, further consideration
will be given to whether the Hub should continue under the current
hosted arrangement or move to an alternative regional delivery
model. This decision does not determine or approve any change to
the legal status, governance or hosting arrangements of the Hub.
Any future proposal to establish, join or participate in a separate
company, legal entity or alternative delivery vehicle would be
subject to further legal, financial and governance advice and would
be brought back through the appropriate decision making route,
including Cabinet where required.
content:
This report seeks approval to proceed with the
proposed enhanced end-to-end model for the Fostering South West
Hub, a regional collaborative arrangement involving local
authorities across the South West which Wiltshire Council jointly
leads with Cornwall Council. The enhanced model builds on the
existing regional marketing and single front door arrangements and
is intended to strengthen foster carer recruitment, assessment,
support and retention across the region. It responds to rising
demand for foster care, increasing complexity of children’s
needs and the need to improve local sufficiency, reduce delay and
support greater placement stability for children.
 
The Cabinet Member is asked to approve
progression of the enhanced Fostering South West Hub model on a
phased basis. Implementation activity will be progressed under
existing officer delegations and in accordance with the
Council’s Constitution, finance, procurement and legal
requirements. As the regional model develops, further consideration
will be given to whether the Hub should continue under the current
hosted arrangement or move to an alternative regional delivery
model. This decision does not determine or approve any change to
the legal status, governance or hosting arrangements of the Hub.
Any future proposal to establish, join or participate in a separate
company, legal entity or alternative delivery vehicle would be
subject to further legal, financial and governance advice and would
be brought back through the appropriate decision making route,
including Cabinet where required.
 

Following consultation
with officers I give notice that I intend to make the decision set
out in the attached report to proceed with the proposed enhanced
end-to-end model for the Fostering South
West Hub.
 
If you would like to
make any representations to me on this issue please do so by 27 August 2026.
 

The proposed decision
will ensure that Wiltshire Council continues to play a leading role
in strengthening regional foster carer recruitment, assessment,
support and retention.
 
Nationally, there is a
shortage of approved foster carers and Government has set out an
ambition to increase the number of foster homes available for
children. Regionally, the Fostering South
West Hub has already established strong foundations through
a coordinated marketing approach and single front door for
prospective foster carers. The enhanced model will build on this
platform by providing a more connected fostering journey from
initial enquiry through assessment, approval and post-approval
support.
 
The enhanced model is
intended to improve progression from enquiry to application and
assessment, reduce drop-off, improve coordination and quality
assurance, strengthen regional data and insight, and support foster
carer retention through a more consistent regional post-approval
offer. It will be implemented on a phased basis, with particular
focus on safe delivery, testing, learning and proportionality.
 
The model will require
continued Department for Education transition funding and financial
contributions from participating local authorities to ensure a
sustainable and effective regional service.
 

The options considered
were:
 

i)              
to approve and continue acting as joint lead for the enhanced
end-to-end Fostering South West Hub;

ii)             
to continue with the Hub in its current recruitment-focused format;
or,

iii)           
to withdraw as co-lead and allow the enhanced model to progress
under the direction of another regional partner.
 
The preferred option
is to approve the enhanced end-to-end model and for Wiltshire
Council to continue to lead this work alongside Cornwall
Council.
 

Information to produce
this paper has been drawn from regional meetings involving senior
officers and Corporate Directors of Children’s Services
across the South West, discussion and guidance from the Department
for Education, local authority sufficiency priorities, operational
learning from the existing Fostering South West Hub and early
design work on the enhanced regional offer.
 
Further implementation
planning will include working groups with local authority
representatives, foster carers and relevant staff across the
region.

Streetscene and Flooding presented a
report seeking the award of the New Term Highways Consultancy

Cllr Smith highlighted the detail contained in the
report in relation to the procurement exercise, details of the contract, the
tender assessment process and the new contract ensuring continuity
of service and allowing the Council to deliver its statutory duties
as highway authority.

 
Cllr Richard Clewer, Leader of the Conservative
Group, commented on concerns he had about the current
contract.

the contract would be delivered bearing in mind that the contract
came in with a lower price.

Director - Place and the Cabinet Member for Highways,
Streetscene and Flooding, to satisfy

take all necessary steps to enter into

1.   
There is a need for a specialist consultant to
provide highway consultancy services and assistance to the Council
when the existing contract ends on 30 November 2026.
 
2.   
Following a procurement exercise in accordance
with the ‘Restricted Procedure’ tenders were submitted
by four companies.

 
3.   
The tenders were assessed in terms of price,
quality, sustainability and social value, and the preferred bidder
has been identified and recommended for acceptance.

 
4.   
The procurement process has been carried out in
accordance with the relevant regulations and Council procedures.
The most advantageous tender for the Council, taking into account quality, sustainability and
social value commitments and price, should be accepted in
accordance with the procurement procedures.

 
5.   
There are processes in place to monitor the
performance of the successful consultant, and for incentivising
performance by the potential award of extensions to the contract
for up to an additional four years.

content:
Resolved:
 

That Cabinet notes:

 


The summary and update on Salisbury Cultural
Quarter in the context of wider infrastructure and regeneration
projects delivered through the Salisbury Central Area
Framework.


 


The recent award of £3 million from Arts
Council England’s (ACE) Creative Foundations Fund to
Wiltshire Creative towards phase 1 only of the Stage the Future
programme, and progress made in securing additional funding to
support delivery of the scheme;


 


The ongoing development of proposals to improve
the Malthouse Lane public realm through the use
of eligible Section 106 funding.


 

That Cabinet approves:

 


The inclusion of Salisbury Cultural Quarter on
the council’s Infrastructure List, recognising its role as
cultural, community and public realm infrastructure that supports
the continued vitality, attractiveness and sustainable growth of
Salisbury;


 


The allocation of £1 million of Strategic
Community Infrastructure Levy funding towards eligible first phase
infrastructure elements of the Stage the Future programme to
renovate and modernise Salisbury Playhouse;

Climate, in consultation with the Cabinet Member for Finance, to
approve the entry into a grant agreement with Wiltshire Creative
for the provision of £1 million Strategic CIL funding towards
phase 1 of the Stage the Future programme;

Climate, in consultation with the Cabinet Member for Finance and
the Director of Legal and Governance, and subject to confirmation
of compliance with the relevant legal and financial requirements,
to enter into a suitable agreement with Wiltshire Creative to
provide an underwriting commitment of up to £3 million in
support of the organisation’s fundraising campaign associated
with phase 1 of the Stage the Future programme.

 
Reason for
Decisions:
 
The
purpose of these proposals is to support the objectives of the
Salisbury
Central Area Framework by:
 

•      
improving the vitality and attractiveness of the
city centre through investment in the Salisbury Cultural
Quarter;

•      
strengthening connectivity between the Cultural
Quarter, Fisherton Street and The Maltings; and

 

•      
securing significant third-party investment and
wider economic, social and environmental benefits that build on the
success of other city centre regeneration projects.

purpose:
(i)

content:
(i)         
Consider comments and objections to the advertised proposals for
amendments to the Traffic Regulation Orders (TROs) applicable to on
and off-street pay and display areas in Wiltshire.
 
(ii)        Recommend the
making of the Orders with amendments.

Following consultation with officers I give
notice that I intend to make the decision set out in the attached
report. If you would like to make any representations to me on this
issue please do so by 15 July 2026.

Following full consideration of all
consultation responses received, alongside the wider operational,
financial, and traffic management implications, the proposed
approach represents a balanced and evidence-led outcome.
 
The recommended changes ensure that parking
tariffs are updated to reflect inflationary increases over the past
four years, while remaining mindful of the historic evidence on how
such changes impact car park usage. At the same time, the approach
responds proportionately to stakeholder feedback, particularly
where concerns were raised about the blanket application of
extended charging hours and Sunday charging across all
locations.
 
The targeted introduction of extended charging
hours and alignment of Sunday charges within short stay car parks
is intended to support retail vitality by encouraging turnover of
spaces and improving accessibility to town and city centres. In
contrast, the continued promotion of long stay car parks for
longer-duration visits is designed to help reduce congestion and
support a more efficient distribution of parking demand.
 
Where specific local factors apply, such as at
Dunns Lane car park in Castle Combe, modifications to the general
approach have been included to support effective traffic
management, particularly during peak visitor periods.
 
The decision also reflects a pragmatic
response to concerns raised regarding the introduction of on-street
Sunday charging, with proposals in certain locations not being
taken forward. Similarly, the adjustment to Sunday charging in long
stay car parks balances the need for income alignment with the
concerns expressed during consultation.
 
In addition, maintaining season ticket pricing
in line with advertised Traffic Regulation Orders ensures continued
value for regular users, while reflecting necessary uplifts. The
introduction of charging in selected facility management car parks
will improve public access and ensure that operational costs are
appropriately recovered.
 
Finally, the implementation of all other
advertised proposals ensures consistency and delivery of the wider
programme. A further comprehensive review of parking arrangements
in Salisbury will be undertaken following the conclusion of the
Park & Ride review, ensuring that future decisions are informed
by a holistic understanding of the network.
 
The decision follows full compliance with the
Traffic Regulation Order consultation process and decision-making
requirements.

(i)       Implement the TROs
as advertised.
 
(ii)       Not implement the
TROs.
 
(iii)      Implement the TROs with
amendments.

Public consultation was undertaken on the
proposed TROs between 9 April and 5 May 2026. Engagement meetings
were carried out with City, Town and Parish Councils prior to this
date. Additional meetings were also held with the Salisbury
Business Improvement District group.

A report was taken to

30 June 2026 and in accordance with the Town and Country Planning
(Local Planning) (England) Regulations 2026, of the timetable and
Notice of Intention to Commence the Wiltshire Local Plan,
confirming that the Plan will incorporate the Minerals and Waste

In order to implement

the Wiltshire Local Plan is approved and the timetable is published
alongside the Notice of Intention to Commence plan preparation,
Cabinet delegated authority to the Director of Planning, Economy
and Climate, in consultation with the Director for Legal and
Governance and Cabinet Member for Strategic Planning to take all
necessary steps for the publication of the Local Plan timetable,

Intention to Commence the Wiltshire Local Plan.
 
In accordance with the

Commence local plan preparation (Regulations 4, 6, 8, 19 and
88[1])

Regulations 4 and 6 of the regulations[2]
and section 15B of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004
(as amended), and statement the timetable is to have effect via the
following means:

o  
On the council’s website (via new suite of Wiltshire Local
Plan webpages)

o  
In the council’s principal office at County Hall,
Trowbridge

o  
At other locations the council deems appropriate, namely Monkton
Park Chippenham and Bourne Hill Salisbury

-      
Publish Notice of Intention to Commence Local Plan preparation,
prepared in accordance with Regulation 19 of the regulations, via
the following means:

Trowbridge

requirements

The decision relates to the outcome of due diligence undertaken on
the Waste Capital Programme, focusing on revised fleet
requirements, updated capital values, procurement phasing, and the
approval of purchase orders needed to secure replacement vehicle
build slots. Two purchase orders are proposed: one to replace 7 x
16T recycling duos in 2026/27 and the second to replace the 7 x 12T
Open back Residual/Garden vehicles in 2027/28. The approach
reflects work to reduce overall capital exposure and phase
investment across multiple financial years while maintaining
service resilience.  Purchase has been
split in this way for these vehicles are 16T recycling duos are
more specialist vehicles, therefore it is imperative to replace
these. 
 

Since the original capital bid, assumptions underpinning fleet
requirements have changed. Following procurement work and evidence
from the Chippenham trial, the Council confirmed retention of a
twin-stream recycling model rather than introducing three-stream
collections. Combined with confidence in the new Materials Recovery
Facility and changes to collection frequencies, vehicle numbers
broadly align with the existing fleet, with only modest
adjustments. Asset life assumptions have also been revised,
spreading the minimum revenue provision over eight years. Planned
electric vehicle purchases for smaller vehicles can no longer
proceed due to insufficient depot charging infrastructure,
resulting in diesel vehicles being specified, with the potential to
use HVO subject to revenue funding.
 

Capital allocation for replacement vehicles was agreed in December
2025 and totals £34.8m including contingency, phased over
several years. Two purchase orders totalling approximately
£2.9m are required by 25 June to secure build slots for
narrow recycling and residual/garden vehicles, with spend remaining
within approved capital allocations. Further rounds modelling may
reduce vehicle numbers, with build slots easier to release than to
add. Ancillary vehicles will be procured separately and brought

To approve and sign an extension of the
contract with The Occasional Kitchen to supply food during Summer
2026 FUEL camps (Wiltshire’s Holiday Activity and Food
Programme).


The council had a contract with the abovenamed providers for the
supply of food in relation to the council’s FUEL programme, a
Department for Education funded programme, which expired following
the end of the Winter 2024 provision.

 

Funding for the 2025 programme was confirmed by the Department for
Education on 20th January 2025, but the exact sum was
not confirmed. Consequently, the timescales required to tender the
service would not enable a service at Easter 2025.

 

The process for setting up a Dynamic Purchase System (DPS) to award
activity provisions on a regular basis following confirmation of
funding was underway in January 2025. This is an extensive
procedure that utilises resource from the Development Team, the
Procurement Team and the Legal team. The timescales for tendering
activity provision did not enable a service at Easter 2025.

 

Contracts for activities at Easter 2025 were awarded based on
exemptions. (Exemption 1332, as approved on 4th February
2025).

 

The contract for the food supplier was awarded on an exemption for
a one-year contract, extendable by three years, dependent on
funding. This allowed the contract to align to the lifetime of the
DPS. (Exemption 1333, as approved on 4th February
2025)

 

The initial one-year contract with the food supplier expired on
19th March 2025.

 

The Department for Education confirmed a three-year funding
agreement in December 2025. This funding is ringfenced and will
fund the Holiday Activity and Food Programme to the end of the
financial year 28/29.

 

The 2026 programme was scheduled to commence on 30 March 2026.

 

The food supplier notified the council that there were potential
changes within the organisation for 2026. They offered assurance
that they could fulfil the requirements of the Easter delivery
window.

 

The contract for the food supplier was extended to cover the Easter
school holiday and reviewed after that delivery window.

 

Following the review after Easter, requirements for the
Summer programme were discussed with the
food supplier and assurance given that they could be met.

 

The contract for the food supplier will be extended to cover the
Summer school holiday period and will be
reviewed again after that delivery window.

process do not allow sufficient time to deliver a service at Summer
2026.
The initial one-year

Cease the service


We would not be able

quality food provision.

returned to the DfE.
Not offering this
programme would increase the vulnerabilities of families on lower
incomes, and result in reputational damage to the council.

content:
To consider the representations
received in response to the advertisement of a Traffic Regulation
Order (TRO hereafter) proposing a 7.5 tonne prohibition of goods
vehicles restriction on the A3098 High Street / Lodge Hill in
Chapmanslade, and to recommend an appropriate way
forward.  


INTENTION TO MAKE DECISION
 
Following consultation with officers I give
notice that I intend to make the decision set out in the attached
report. If you would like to make any representations to me on this
issue, please do so by 2 July 2026.

Introducing a 7.5 tonne prohibition of goods
vehicles restriction on the A3098 High Street / Lodge Hill will
improve road safety and help protect the environment in
Chapmanslade.
 
The proposal is intended to reduce the number
of inappropriate heavy goods vehicles using the village as a
through route, which is causing damage to the road surface and
verges and obstructing traffic flow on the narrow roads. Access for
loading and unloading to adjacent businesses and premises within
the restricted area will remain unaffected.
 
The proposed TRO meets priorities 2, 3, 6, and
7 identified in the Council’s ‘Our Wiltshire Plan
2025-2035’.

To:
 

1.   
Implement the proposal as advertised.

2.   
Abandon the proposal.

Consultation has been undertaken with:
 

·      
The elected Wiltshire Council member through the
statutory TRO process.

·      
Chapmanslade Parish Council through the statutory
TRO process.

·      
Emergency Services through the statutory TRO
process.

·      
Members of the public through the statutory TRO
process.
 
The proposed TRO was subject to formal
consultation from 13 March to 6 April 2026.
 
During this period, a total of 88
representations were received. Of these, 85 were in support of the
proposal and 3 objected to the proposal. 
 
A plan illustrating the proposal is provided
in Appendix 1. A summary of the correspondence received,
together with officer responses to the comments, is set out in
Appendix 2.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Highways, Streetscene, and Flooding has decided to implement a 7.5 tonne prohibition of goods vehicles restriction in Chapmanslade to improve road safety and protect the environment.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Highways, Streetscene, and Flooding
purpose:
In response to feedback received from some
Councillors around extended project delivery timescales and limited
resources, and in light of proposed
changes to the Area Boards, Cabinet expressed a desire to review
the functionality of Local Highways & Footway Improvement
Groups (LHFIGs) and consider whether changes should be made to the
future operation of the LHFIGs.
content:
In response to feedback received from some
Councillors around extended project delivery timescales and limited
resources, and in light of proposed
changes to the Area Boards, Cabinet expressed a desire to review
the functionality of Local Highways & Footway Improvement
Groups (LHFIGs) and consider whether changes should be made to the
future operation of the LHFIGs.
 

Following consultation with officers I give
notice that I intend to make the decision set out in the attached
report. If you would like to make any representations to me on this
issue, please do so by 25 June 2026
 

Continuing with the LHFIGs in their current
format would continue to allow local involvement and the delivery
of community schemes.  This has a proven
track record and would as likely remain successful.  However, it would not address the concerns that
have been raised.  The move to greater
funding of Substantive schemes, with a continuation at the current
level in funding direct to the groups, would address the concerns
raised through the survey.  There is
however a need to correctly spend the available funding and help
secure future financial allocations from the DfT and CIL. This can
be addressed by use of a tick box business case that ensures that
requests align with LTP objectives. 
Staffing resource levels are an area of concern and
will need to be monitored.  However, the
proposed process changes are intended to help address some of the
concerns in this area.
 
Changes to process and procedure are required
to ensure the LHFIGs align with the proposed Area Board changes and
remain an efficient and effective way of delivering community led
schemes.
 

Two options have been considered
 
Option 1 - That the LHFIGs and Substantive
schemes continue in their current funding format with changes to
process and procedure.
 
Groups £500K, Substantive schemes £250K
Introduction of Price list
Reintroduction of five live schemes and prioritised scheme
pipeline
Process flow charts and Form of Delegation
Revised Terms of Reference and Guidance notes
Record of compliance with funding requirements
Substantive bid process would remain an annual event.
From 27/28
introduce a defined minimum local contribution.
 
Option 2 - That the LHFIGs and Substantive
schemes continue with an increase to funding for substantive
schemes, improvements to process and procedure.
 
Groups £500K, Substantive schemes increased budget circa
£500K
Introduction of Price list
Reintroduction of five live schemes and prioritised scheme
pipeline
Process flow charts and Form of Delegation
Revised Terms of Reference and Guidance notes
Record of compliance with funding requirements
Substantive bid process would become a biannual
event.
From 27/28
introduce a defined minimum local contribution
 

To gain a comprehensive understanding of the
concerns, a survey was undertaken in December 2025 with a
questionnaire being sent to all Wiltshire Councillors and all Town
and Parish Councils.  The purpose of the
survey was to assess perceptions of the effectiveness of the
LHFIGs, to identify strengths, weaknesses, and opportunities for
improvement and to inform future policy, process, and resourcing
decisions.
 
Survey results
 
The survey collected a total of 133
responses.  Of these 80 were from Parish
Councils, 37 from Wiltshire Councillors, and 16 from Town
Councils.  Representation was received
from across all 18 community areas.
 
The survey results highlighted the key
achievements in terms of scheme delivery including 20mph limits,
traffic calming and pedestrian safety schemes, drop kerbs and
accessibility improvements, and sign, road marking and Speed
Indicator Device infrastructure. 
Feedback indicated that the LHFIGs are valued and locally
relevant.
 
The survey identified a
number of key concerns for further
consideration.  These included slow
delivery times and lengthy process, limited officer capacity and
high workload, contractor performance and cost pressures and
complexity of legal order process, and where formal assessments are
required.  Feedback indicated that
clarifying and simplifying some processes would be beneficial.
 
Contained within the survey was the suggestion
of an alternative mechanism for costing certain types of schemes by
use of a price list approach.  This
would speed up the process by reducing the need for a bespoke cost
estimates to be prepared by officers prior to funding approval from
the group and contributing bodies.  This
was overwhelmingly supported (114 responses).
 
There was a strong preference for local
financial contributions to schemes to remain at the discretion of
the individual groups rather than imposing a blanket approach.
 
There was majority support to increase the
number of ‘Substantive’ schemes being undertaken and to
increase the number of bidding rounds
each year. Alongside this, concerns were expressed about complexity
and bureaucracy of the current bidding process.
 
A copy of the Questionnaire and a summary of
responses is included at Appendix A.

2026.

dualling scheme (phases 4 and 5) having already completed the
previous phases. This scheme originated from the longstanding
priority to improve north-south connectivity along the A350, and
Wiltshire Council has been progressively bringing forward the
dualling of the A350 Chippenham bypass.

·      
Reduce journey times along the A350 Chippenham Bypass

·      
Improve average speeds and decrease congestion at pinch-point
locations such as the Bumpers Farm Roundabout

·      
Improve safety and reduce traffic collisions along the A350
Chippenham Bypass
 
The proposals are in accordance with Theme 3
in Wiltshire Council’s Business Plan 2022-2032.

Implement the proposals as advertised.

Amend the proposals in consideration of the comments received.
(iii)         
Abandon the proposals.

·      
The elected Wiltshire Council Members representing Chippenham,

Chippenham Town Council through the statutory consultation
process

Emergency services through the statutory consultation process

·      
Members of the public and local
residents, through the statutory consultation process.
         
TROs proposing the speed limit changes for the
A350 in Chippenham were formally advertised for comment on 30th
April 2026. The Council's closing date for the receipt of
objections or other representations to the advertised TROs,
together with the grounds on which they were made, was 1st June
2026.
 
During the consultation period, a total of
eighteen items of correspondence were received in response to the
Council’s proposal. All eighteen items were, at least in some
part, related to the various proposed speed limit changes on the
A350 Chippenham. Eight of the eighteen items also raised issues
outside the scope of the Council’s proposal or contained no
outright objection or support. Of the eighteen items, 8 were from
residents opposed to some or all speed limit changes proposed
(including one comment of opposition supported by a Parish
council), two items supported the scheme outright.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Highways, Streetscene, and Flooding
purpose:
To consider the outcome of the
informal consultation at the five-pilot location for School
Streets, and determine which, if any, should be progressed to
implementation under an Experimental Traffic Regulation Order
(ETRO).
content:
To consider the outcome of the
informal consultation at the five-pilot location for School
Streets, and determine which, if any, should be progressed to
implementation under an Experimental Traffic Regulation Order
(ETRO).

INTENTION TO MAKE
DECISION
 
Following consultation with officers I give
notice that I intend to make the decision as follows:
 
That:
 

(i)   
School Streets be implemented under an ETRO in the locations
specified in Melksham, Warminster, Calne.

(ii)  
Queens Crescent be given further time to develop an alternative,
supported Park and Stride location to alleviate local concerns;

(iii) 
Consideration is given at a later date in Staverton and that prior
to this investigation is made into potential highway improvement
measures to improve the perception of road safety for those
walking, wheeling and cycling to the two schools.

(iv) 
Approve the list of legitimate exemptions, in addition to those
statutory to a Traffic Regulation Order.
 
If you would like to make any representations
to me on this issue please do so by 8 June 2026.

Many schools experience the inconvenience and
risks associated with a high level of parking and vehicle
manoeuvres at the beginning and end of the school day.  It is considered that a school street could be an
additional measure to assist schools in addressing these concerns
to assist in developing a formal policy, it was considered a pilot
should be undertaken to determine future methods of identifying
suitable schools sites.
 
Three sites provided substantial support for a
school street; these are Aloeric Primary School in Melksham,
Fynamore Primary School in Calne and Minster Primary School in
Warminster. It is considered that these should be progressed
 
At Queen’s Crescent School in
Chippenham, there has been a level of objection from those
residents living outside the proposed extent of the school street,
and the owner of the car park which is currently used as a
park-and-stride location, and has been for an extended period of
time, does not wish the car park to be promoted as part of the
school street proposals.  The school is
currently researching alternative facilities to allay some of these
concerns and should an alternative location be found by the end of
June, it is proposed that Queen’s Crescent is included in the
pilot cohort. If a viable alternative is not identified, the
location should be held in abeyance.
 
Substantive concerns were raised by residents
in Staverton which centre around access for carers and
deliveries.  The Primary School have
attempted to alleviate these and proposed a change in the extent of
the school street so that it commences west of the entrance to the
school car park, with those parents at it, and the neighbouring
Emmaus School, who wish to continue to drive to school being able
to drive through the car park to drop / collect their child(ren)
from the schools.  Upon review, it is
considered this is contrary to the ethos of the key school street
aim, which is to provide a significant reduction in vehicular
traffic in the road(s) leading to a school site. School Streets are
intended to provide environmental, safety and perceptual changes so
that there is greater confidence in walking, wheeling and cycling
to engrain positive attitudes to sustainable travel
methods.  Consequently, it is proposed
that the Staverton site is not included in the initial cohort of
school streets but that the feasibility of mitigating engineering
measures is investigated as a first step through the Taking Acton
on School Journey initiative. This would not preclude
reconsideration as future site, should the pilot be considered
successful.

To:

(i)   
Implement a school street at each of the five sites with the
proposed permissible exemptions.

(ii)  
Implement a school street at each of those sites where the
consultation results give a clear message of support with the
proposed permissible exemptions.

(iii) 
Implement a school street at none of the sites.

The following consultation has been
undertaken:
 

A briefing session for elected
members on Microsoft teams was held on 14 October 2025;
A briefing session for parish
councils on Microsoft teams was held on 15 October 2025;
Informal consultation took place
over a six-week period from 2 November to 14 December 2026
involving local residents and businesses along with members of the
school community.  The primary method
for gathering feedback was via the “Commonplace”
digital platform. A total of 5528 leaflets were distributed across
the proposed school street areas with information about the
proposal and how to provide feedback;
In-person pop-up events were held at
schools during termtime to discuss the proposals with parents and
carers, and to provide further opportunity for individual
feedback;
Additional meetings were arranged to
discuss the proposals with Beeches Veterinary Centre on 11 November
2025 in Melksham and Nestlings Pre-School on 26 November 2025 in
Staverton;
Social media posts were distributed
on Instagram, Facebook, X (Twitter) and LinkedIn providing
information and updates about the proposal, along with
opportunities to provide feedback.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Highways, Streetscene, and Flooding has decided to implement School Streets in three pilot locations, with one location given more time to develop an alternative solution, and another location not included in the initial cohort.

The proposals are primarily focused upon the
promotion of increased independence for young people, supporting
their preparedness for adulthood. It is anticipated that there

taxi provision to more independent travel via travel assistance and
access to public transport or parental supported
transport.
 
A saving of £406k for the 26/27 and a further

MTFS.
 
Reduce the Council’s expenditure on external
taxi providers over the next few years, where Post 16 learners on
transport (per current Policy) is forecast to grow.

decision_maker: Deputy Leader of the Council and Cabinet Member for Communities, Engagement, and Corporate Services
purpose:
This report seeks authority to implement the
amendments to Area Board arrangements as reviewed and
discussed through following a recent consultation process with
Area Board Chairs and others.
content:
This report seeks authority to implement the
amendments to Area Board arrangements as reviewed and
discussed through following a recent consultation process with
Area Board Chairs and others. 

I give notice that I
intend to implement the changes to the Area Board arrangements as
set out within the supporting documents below.  
 
If you would like to
make any representations to me on this issue, please do so
by 12 May 2026.
 

In accordance
with the Constitution Area Boards allocate their
funds, and operate their procedures, in accordance
with procedural rules and guidance as issued from time to time
by the Leader.  
 
Those procedures have
not been updated in full since May 2022, with the relevant Cabinet Member further
updating grant funding criteria in March 2025. It is therefore appropriate
to have undertaken a review of the arrangements to ensure
they remain up to date, effective, and
consistent.  
 

Following an evidence based review
and extensive engagement with Area Board Chairs and others,
the changes proposed are proposed to provide additional
guidance on Area Board arrangements, encourage community
based events and activities through the Area Board framework,
and update procedures and delegation requirements to increase
efficiency and effectiveness. 
 
The Leader
has designated the Deputy Leader as the Cabinet Member
with responsibility for Area Boards, including updating the Area
Board handbook, other procedures,
and delegations requirements. 
 

Potential alternative
adjustments to aspects of the procedures
or delegations were discussed at the multiple sessions of
Area Board Chairs, as well as the potential to make no updates to
any of the procedures. This included detailed discussions on
structure of formal meetings, frequency and type of meetings,
delegation requirements, branding and naming of Area Boards, and
seeking other suggestions on a cross-party basis on how to improve
effectiveness and engagement. 
 
Given the amount of
time since the last full review of the arrangements it
was not considered appropriate to not update the
arrangements.
 

The proposed changes have been discussed
with the Overview and Scrutiny Management
Committee Chairman in January 2026. 
 
The proposals have been discussed and
consulted on during September 2025, January 2026, and March 2026,
through the Area Board Chair and Vice Chair
meetings.  
 
A separate Overview and Scrutiny Task Group
has been set up to review the Area Board Grant Funding model,
following the Management Committee meeting in March 2026. 
 
A wide range of stakeholders were
consulted during September, October and November 2025, to
inform and shape the new Area Board arrangements. A summary of
this consultation can be found within
appendix B.
topline: The Deputy Leader of the Council has decided to implement amendments to Area Board arrangements following a recent consultation process.

INTENTION TO MAKE DECISION
 
Following consultation with officers I give
notice that I intend to make the decision to write-off of
£180,000 capital loan and £11,615.53 loan interest
(revenue) owed by Fays Flowers Ltd as part of the Growing Place
Infrastructure Fund (GPIF) loan programme following the company
going into administration and later being dissolved.  If you would like to make any representations to
me on this issue please do so by Tuesday 12 May 2026.

The company has dissolved and Wiltshire
Council has been informed that, as a creditor, none of the money
owed will be returned to it.

Fays Flowers appointed a voluntary liquidator
on 16 January 2025.  The debt to
Wiltshire Council was registered with the administrators and the
company creditor paperwork was filed within the required
deadlines.  The company was wound up by
the administrators on 19 August 2025; no funds were left in the
business to distribute to registered creditors.  The company was dissolved at Companies House
(Company number 08940704) on 21 November 2025.
 
Fays Flowers owed £180,000 in capital
payments and £11,615.53 in interest.  These sums need to be formally written off from
Council’s accounts recognising that the loan will not be
repaid. 

Not applicable.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Finance has decided to write off a £180,000 capital loan and £11,615.53 loan interest owed by Fays Flowers Ltd as part of the Growing Place Infrastructure Fund loan programme.

There needs to be a mechanism for delivering
Area Board transport scheme priorities that exceed the Area
Board’s available discretionary highway budget and are unable
to be implemented in phases over time. The agreed methodology and
application of the Substantive Highway Scheme Bid Evaluation
Formula has resulted in eleven scheme bids being ranked and five
awarded Substantive Highway Scheme funding in the 2025/26 financial
year.

Eleven bids were received in this bidding
round, totalling £750,139, and requesting a total of
£571,286. This exceeds the proposed allocation of
£250,000 for the Substantive Highway Scheme Fund in 2025/26.
All of the bids have been scored using the Substantive Highway
Scheme Bid Evaluation Formula which ranks the schemes according to
cost-benefit and deliverability.  It is
proposed that Substantive Highway Scheme funds the top five bids,
totalling £209,986.  The results
are set out in Appendix 2.

The Cabinet Member report that outlined and
approved the mechanism for applying for Substantive Highway Scheme
funding was circulated to all Members and Community Area Managers
in July 2011. In addition, informal consultation on the Substantive
Highway Scheme funding mechanism and discussion on the opportunity
to bid for funding has taken place at the Local Highway &
Footway Improvement Group meetings since that time.

content:
The council declared a
Climate Emergency in February 2019 and committed to seeking to make
Wiltshire carbon-neutral by 2030.

Delivery of the Business Plan 2025–2035 is supported by
action that enables residents and organisations to adopt low-carbon
technologies and contribute to a more sustainable, resilient
Wiltshire. The Switch Together programme aligns with the Business
Plan’s focus on a sustainable environment, promoting
investment in renewable energy, strengthening local energy
resilience, and encouraging community participation in
carbon-reduction activity. By facilitating access to affordable
solar PV and battery storage through a trusted route, participation
in upcoming schemes, helps advance the council’s long-term
aims for a greener, more energy-independent county.

Implementation of the Climate Strategy is progressed through
initiatives that accelerate renewable energy generation and improve
the performance of Wiltshire’s buildings. The scheme supports
two of the Strategy’s core themes—Energy and Homes
& the Built Environment—by expanding rooftop solar
generation, increasing local clean-energy capacity, and helping
households cut emissions. The approach also reflects the
Strategy’s emphasis on partnership working and large-scale
engagement, providing a practical mechanism for residents to take
meaningful climate action and contributing towards
Wiltshire’s ambition to become carbon-neutral by 2030.

Wiltshire has successfully delivered four previous schemes,
enabling more than 2,000 households to install solar panels and
battery storage, supported by over £17M of private
investment, generating a total installed capacity of 8MW and
delivering an estimated 39,000 tonnes of CO2 savings over 25 years.
Scheme 3 (2024) achieved average annual bill reductions of
£495 per household.

Switch Together provides a trusted, council-endorsed route for
residents, businesses and community groups to access high-quality
solar PV and battery installations at competitive prices through a
vetted, collective-purchasing model.

The council and iChoosr jointly promote the scheme to households
who are most likely to benefit, using targeted, co-branded
communications, before iChoosr conducts a reverse auction to secure
a qualified installer offering the lowest priced compliant
bid.

Residents can register without commitment, receive a personalised
quote after the auction, and proceed only if their property is
assessed as suitable, ensuring a simple, managed low-risk process
supported by economies of scale.

Benefits of participating in Switch Together Solar

Benefits to residents are:
• Low-cost solar PV and battery storage through group
buying
• Trusted, vetted installers and quality assurance
• Simple hassle-free process from registration to installation
and post installation support
• Meaningful reductions in household energy bills
• Increased energy independence and security which can protect
from price shocks
• Insurance-backed guarantees and consumer protection
• Proven scheme with a large and international track
record
• An opportunity to contribute to tackling the climate
emergency

The benefits to the council are:
• Advances the council’s Business Plan and strategic
objectives, including delivery of the Climate Strategy and progress
toward a carbon-neutral Wiltshire by 2030.
• Delivers measurable carbon-reduction outcomes through
large-scale uptake of rooftop solar and battery storage.
• Operates on a cost-neutral delivery model, with scheme fees
offsetting the cost of officer time, marketing and administrative
costs.
• Unlocks substantial private investment into Wiltshire,
driving the growth of local renewable capacity without requiring
council capital funding.
• Stimulates economic activity in the green energy
sector.
• Enhances public trust in renewable energy incentives by
providing a vetted council-endorsed route to high-quality
installations.
• Reduces operational burden for the council, as iChoosr
manages supplier vetting, installer procurement, customer handling
and quality assurance.
• Minimises resident-facing demand on council services, with
iChoosr providing customer support with historically low levels of
complaints.
• Builds community engagement and climate literacy, helping
residents understand and adopt low-carbon technologies.
• Enables a small amount of officer time to deliver high
impact, leveraging staff capacity to facilitate carbon savings and
private investment.

Risks and Mitigations - see attached document.

Implications
Staffing: Staffing implications are limited to officer time within
the Climate and Communications team functions to support promotion,
coordination and oversight of the scheme. No additional posts are
required, and the contract enables recovery of staffing and
promotional costs through scheme fees. IChoosr’s management
of installer vetting, customer support and quality assurance
further reduces operational burden on council staff.

Financial: Participation in the scheme is expected to be
cost-neutral, as scheme fee income is designed to cover the
councils direct marketing and administrative costs. The peak
requirement of approximately 1.5 officer days a week during the
promotional period (6-9 weeks) and around 0.5 days a week during
the installation phase. The financial risk is limited and mitigated
by the schemes established track record and use of cost recovery
fee structure. The council does not handle any resident payments,
as all financial transactions occur between the resident, iChoosr
and the installer.

Legal: The concession contract with iChoosr has been reviewed
through the councils legal and procurement processes to ensure
compliance with procurement, contracting and data-protection
requirements. Procurement services have confirmed that the council
is not required to run a tender procedure to award this contract.
Data sharing arrangements comply with GDPR, with iChoosr
responsible for managing all registration data. There are no
anticipated legal barriers to entering into the contract

content:
To approve the
freehold purchase of Trowbridge Hospital at a value of
[Redacted].

The NHS
have put the Trowbridge Hospital site on the market being a circa
3 acre site via Alder King, following
completion of the Integrated Care Centre on the adjacent site. The
Council has submitted a best and final bid for the site, see Annex
A, which has been accepted by the NHS. Heads of Terms are being
prepared for the acquisition and this
decision is in advance of these.
 
The
Council’s interest in the site is for the delivery of a care
home, with capital up to £1.700m approved at Full Council on
21 October 2025. The bid submitted was at [redacted] on an
unconditional basis and completion is required by 30 June 2026. A
valuation of the site has been undertaken, through an external
agent, on the basis of [redacted]
supporting the accepted bid.
 
A
detailed business case to support the purchase of the site was
completed that evidenced the need for care provision of this type
for West Wiltshire. [redacted sentence].
 
The
need for a care home has been established by the Council for the
Trowbridge area; via a review by Adults Commissioning and presented
to Cabinet on 15 October 2025.
 
On
acquisition, the site presents numerous risks to the Council
including holding costs, site security and timescales for holding
the asset – [redacted].
 
The
site has a large number of buildings
present and multiple entry points to the site, meaning that site
access and risks exist.
 
Considerations/Issues/Risks
 
The
site is extensive, comprising a large, dual-fronted footprint with
multiple interconnected and standalone buildings, including a
prominent listed structure that must be retained. The grounds are
substantial, with boundaries adjoining residential properties to
the south, a major road frontage to the north, an NHS facility to
the east, and an existing care home to the west. This complexity
will influence both interim management and future
redevelopment.
If
purchased this would present one of the largest and most complex
sites that the PI&O service has had to managed and a void
site.
 
[4
redacted paragraphs]
 
Financial Implications
 
A bid
of [redacted] be accepted and with the associated costs of SDLT and
legal fees it is not anticipated that the expenditure will exceed
£1.700m
 
Any
surplus funds available could be used to fund the necessary  investigations
to progress with demolition of large parts of the site.
 
Based
on previous experience of holding costs at other sites, the council
should allow a [redacted] to hold the site. This is an estimate of
the cost of security (patrols + mobile CCTV and monitoring),
utilities, and general upkeep. These costs cannot be capitalised
and will be a revenue burden.
 
The
cost of the fencing would need to be added to this figure and if
there is an NNDR liability, this would be in addition to
[redacted]. These costs may not be capable of capitalising and are
likely to be a revenue burden.
 
[redacted paragraph]
 
I
confirm that in making this decision I have considered the
following in line with Wiltshire Council’s
Constitution:
 
Key
decision requirements: Yes

Views of relevant cabinet member(s), committee chairman, area
board(s): Yes – considered as part
of the Cabinet and Full Council approvals

Consultation with cabinet member(s), the Leader and Scrutiny (for
Executive decisions taken under Emergency Powers): NA – not
using Executive Powers.

Consultation in accordance with the council’s consultation
guidance and the views emanating from that process: N/A – although considered as part of the
Cabinet and Full Council approvals

Implication of any council policy, initiative, strategy or
procedure: Yes – the acquisition is
intended to support the emerging Accommodation Strategy from People
Directorate

Staffing, financial and legal implications: Yes –
significant, see section 7-16 of the attached Rood.

associated with the creation of a care home does not materialise
– leading to increased holding costs. There is a risk of
vandalism and antisocial behaviour on the site – immediate
activity needed to secure the site. There is a significant risk

need to dispose of the site

considered as part of the Cabinet and Full Council
approvals

NA

The proposal seeks to
improve conditions for road users and residents with the
implementation of parking controls (No Waiting at Any time) on the
following roads:
 
Noremarsh Road.
Parsons Way, Washbourne Road, Clarendon Drive and Eastwood
Avenue.

content:
At its meeting on 9
December 2025 Cabinet considered a proposal to implement an online
booking system for use with Household Recycling Centres as part of
demand management, helping to reduce queuing, improve customer
service, reduce commercial waste abuse, and provide other
benefits.

The meeting on 9 December 2025 resolved to implement a trial use of
an online booking system at sites in Stanton St Quintin, Salisbury,
Melksham, and Devizes and delegated this to the Director,
Environment.

Purton and Lower Compton HRCs were not included as part of the
trial because at that meeting it had been resolved to not extend
the contract with Hills Waste Solutions Ltd for continued operation
of those sites beyond August 2026, so they would not have been
available as part of any trial.

Subsequently, and following receipt of an improved offer from Hills
Waste Solutions Ltd, Cabinet amended its proposed budget at a
meeting on 3 February 2026 to remove savings from not extending the
contracts to operate Lower Compton and Purton HRC, in anticipation
of extending the contracts for three-year periods. That budget was
approved by Full Council on 24 February 2026, and a formal decision
to extend the contracts was confirmed in delegated decision
ECW-01-26 on 11 March 2026.

The decision to continue operations for Purton and Lower Compton
HRCs is predicated upon development of a new HRC site to serve the
north of Wiltshire from around mid-2029 onwards. This would likely
include a substantial proportion of current usage from the Purton
site and some amount of usage from the Lower Compton site.

Had an extension been agreed at the December meeting, the service
would have requested that the trial would also have been extended
to Purton and Lower Compton HRCs in order to ensure that necessary
information could be gathered at the same time.

The intention to trial use at Purton and Lower Compton HRCs was
also announced at a well-attended public meeting of the Calne Area
Board on 5 February 2026.

It is considered that given the decisions made by Cabinet and Full
Council to extend the contracts for Purton and Lower Compton HRCs
included additional cost of extending the trial to those sites,
that it falls within the Director’s general delegated
authority under the scheme of sub-delegation to agree further sites
for inclusion of the trial of an online booking system. This would
comprise a lawful action consistent with the Director’s area
of responsibility and would deliver upon an agreed policy for
operation and management of the HRCs within the approved
budget.

I confirm that in making this decision I have considered the
following in line with Wiltshire Council’s
Constitution:

Key decision requirements: NA

Views of relevant cabinet member(s), committee chairman, area
board(s):

The Cabinet Member and Leader have agreed inclusion of the areas as
part of the trial.

The intention for both areas to be included as part of the trial of
the online booking system was set out by relevant Cabinet Members
at a meeting of Calne Area Board on 5 February 2026 once it had
been agreed in principle to extend the contracts for Purton and
Lower Compton HRC. A meeting of Royal Wootton Bassett and Cricklade
Area Board took place prior to agreement to extend use of the
current sites and the potential for use of a trial system, however,
as it is presently only a trial that is proposed it is considered
appropriate to proceed.

Consultation with cabinet member(s), the Leader and Scrutiny (for
Executive decisions taken under Emergency Powers): NA

Consultation in accordance with the council’s consultation
guidance and the views emanating from that process: Not applicable
– Cabinet had agreed the principle of trialling an online
booking system at its meeting on 9 December, this decision is
including additional trial sites given follow up Cabinet and Full
Council decisions to retain those sites.

Implication of any council policy, initiative, strategy or
procedure: The inclusion of the sites within the trial will assist
with the agreed approach of developing a new site for the north of
the county.

Staffing, financial and legal implications: The additional cost of
including two further areas within the booking system trial were
included in the extension costs presented in the MTFS agreed at
Full council on 24th February 2026

The assessment of any associated risks in accordance with the
Council’s risk management strategy: Not applicable

Involvement of appropriate statutory officers and/or corporate
directors and directors: The Monitoring Officer and Corporate
Director, Place, have been consulted on this decision.

Regional or national guidance from other bodies where relevant: Not
applicable

The council’s constitution, including the Procurement and
Contract Rules (Part 10) and the Financial Regulations and
Procedure Rules (Part 9), all relevant guidance, legislation, codes
of practice, and protocols: Not applicable

content:
This report outlines the progress made on the
Local Cycling and Walking Infrastructure Plan (LCWIP) for
Calne.  It summarises the work program
and consultation undertaken and seeks member approval for the
LCWIP, and priority schemes put forward for Calne.

Following
consultation with officers I give notice that I intend to make the
decision set out in the attached report.  If you would like to make any representations to
me on this issue, please do so by Thursday 26 March 2026.

Adopted LCWIPs are a key prerequisite for
unlocking government funding through Active Travel England
(ATE).  Failure to develop and adopt
LCWIPs will significantly reduce the chance of successful funding
bids and is likely to harm the Council’s ambitious
aspirations on active travel, climate change, air pollution, and
health and wellbeing objectives.
 

No other options have been
considered.  It is
clear that the government requires all walking and cycling
schemes to be developed as part of a systematic, evidence-based
network of routes using the LCWIP methodology.  Without the provenance of an LCWIP it is unlikely
that any capital scheme bids will be successful in attracting
government capital funding to enable implementation.
 

The LCWIP has been developed through extensive
consultation with local elected members, key stakeholders and the
public.

The LCWIP consultation
was undertaken in three stages, the first was stakeholder
engagement in November 2023 via a Teams meeting, the second was a
full public consultation between 20th November 2023
until 6th February 2024 and the third full publication
consultation was between 16th July and 6th
September 2024. The two full public consultations were undertaken
using the Commonplace website. 
A report of the public consultation summaries is shown in
Appendix 1, with the main points summarised below.

The initial
stakeholder engagement was held via a Teams meeting and introduced
the concept of LCWIPs, an outline of the process, programme and
final outcomes. Following this engagement a site audit was carried
out. The site audit, which included Atkins and Wiltshire Council
officers was undertaken to consider all routes in more detail
within the core study area.

Draft priority routes were prepared following the site audit and a
draft LCWIP report was developed.

The first full public consultation detailed the draft routes and
asked respondents for their feedback about the selected routes as
well as suggestions for alternative routes using an interactive
map.

Using feedback from the consultation and the prioritisation tool
key priority routes were selected.

The second public consultation invited respondents to put in order
of preference the priority routes for order of delivery for
both cycling and walking.
 During
the consultation period, 70 comments were received either via the
Commonplace platform and email. The Commonplace contributions
included written comments or more detailed responses and pins
dropped on the interactive cycling and walking maps.
 
There were no obvious
gaps in participation and so the council is confident that the
level and nature of feedback was strong and appropriate given the
context of the consultation.
 
Key data from the
survey is summarised as follows:
Three priority
corridors were identified for Calne with the aim of delivering
walking, (including wheeling) and cycling improvements along each
of the corridors. Whilst all modes of active travel follow the same
corridor there are some slight variations in actual route for each
of the modes. However, in terms of preferred order of delivery the
results were identical for cycling and walking as follows:
 
Order of cycling priority corridor/route for
delivery -
 

1st – CC01 - Centre
to Tesco on Oxford Road
2nd – CC02 - Centre
to Quemerford
3rd – CC07 Centre
to Sandpit Road

 
Order of walking priority corridor/routes for
delivery -
 

1st – CW07 - Centre
to Tesco on Oxford Road
2nd – CW01 - Centre
to Quemerford
3rd – CW09 Centre
to Sandpit Road

 
Respondents indicated that they do not have a
preferred mode when it comes to spending priority; 46% stated it
should be about the same.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Highways, Streetscene, and Flooding has decided to approve the Local Cycling and Walking Infrastructure Plan (LCWIP) for Calne, including priority schemes for walking and cycling improvements.

purpose:
The North Wessex Downs is seeking grants for
landscape-scale projects to enhance the protected landscape,
including new public access, ponds, hedgerows, woodland and
agroforestry. If successful, the grants would total over £1m
and require Cabinet approval.
content:
Resolved:
 

1.   
That Cabinet approves the North Wessex Downs National Landscape
(NWDNL) request to apply, and if successful, accept multiple grants
from the National Grids Landscape Enhancement Initiative. The grant
amounts collectively will exceed one million pounds in grant
funding for multiple projects across the NWDNL.

 

2.   
That the Director of Environment and the Corporate Director of
Resources, in consultation with the Corporate Director of Place, be
authorised to make and approve any applications to and to approve
for acceptance grants from the National Grid LEI and to approve the
entering into any documentation in
connection therewith including any partnership, procurement or
delivery agreements.
 
Reason for
Decision:
 
The North Wessex Downs National Landscape partnership
has the statutory purposes of conserving and enhancing natural
beauty of the Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty (AONB). Through
seeking funding from the National Grid Landscape Enhancement
Initiative, the NWDNL are upholding their statutory
purpose.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve over one million pounds in grants for projects in the North Wessex Downs National Landscape.

purpose:
The Crisis Resilience Fund (CRF) has been made
available to Local Authorities in England to support low-income
households who encounter financial shock and to support activity
that builds individual and community financial resilience. This
report provides a summary of the fund and requests delegation of
the payment criteria.
content:
Resolved:
 
That Cabinet:
 

1.   
Notes the content of the report

 

2.   
Delegates the payment criteria to the Corporate Director of
Place and Corporate Director of Resources in consultation with the
Cabinet Member for Communities, Partnerships, Engagement,
Libraries, Leisure, Culture, Corporate Services, Governance and
Operational Services.

 

3.   
Approves the cessation of the council’s Local Welfare
Payment scheme, on the basis that its core purposes—issuing
emergency payments to support residents with fuel, food, and
essential white goods—will be both replicated and
strengthened within the Crisis Payments component of the CRF
scheme.
 
Reason for
Decision:
 
To inform Cabinet of the Crisis Resilience Fund
awarded by the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local
Government and to enable suitable investment of the fund that will
support Wiltshire households.

content:
The purpose of this report is to ask the
Cabinet Member to agree the school term and holiday dates for
2027/28 for Wiltshire’s Community, Voluntary Controlled and
Community Special Schools.
 

INTENTION TO MAKE
DECISION
 
Following consultation with officers I give
notice that I intend to make the decision set out in the attached
report. If you would like to make any representations to me on this
issue please do so by  23 March
2026.
 

As
dictated by Section 32 of the Education Act 2002, the local
authority is responsible for determining the term dates for all
community, voluntary controlled or community special schools in
Wiltshire.
 

Options Considered
(Appendix A)
 
Option 1: Shows a proposed
calendar provided a shorter summer holiday and a seven-day October
half term and an early Easter break with term 6 ending on Tuesday
25 July 2028.
 
Option 2: Shows a proposed
calendar provided a marginally longer summer holiday and a seven
day October half term and a later Easter break with term 6 ending
Monday 24 July 2028.
 
Option 3: Shows a proposed
calendar provided a longer summer holiday and a five-day October
break and later Easter break with term 6 ending Friday 21 July

content:
Following agreement of the financial context
by Full Council as recommended by Cabinet, it is proposed to
formally rescind Proposal 5 of Minute 76 of the meeting of Cabinet
held on 9 December 2025:
 
“to not take
up the extension option with Hills Waste Services for the provision
and operation of two provider owned Household Recycling Centres and
close the two sites, Lower Compton and Purton, from August 2026 at
the end of the current contract period”.
 
In order to give effect to resolution L of
Minute 30 of the meeting of Cabinet held on 3 February 2026 (Amend
proposed budget to remove HRC closure savings), following approval
by Full Council, I intend to agree the following:
 

1)   
To extend the contract with Hills Waste Services for the
provision and operation of the Purton HRC from August 2026 on a 3
year + 1 year extension basis; and,

 

2)   
To extend the contract with Hills Waste Services for the
provision and operation of the Lower Compton HRC from August 2026
on a 1 year + 1 year + 1 year basis
 
This would not preclude the potential of
further extensions being agreed if this was considered economically
feasible and desirable. Such extensions could not go beyond July
2034, as defined in the contract.

Following consultation with officers and
council’s decision to approve the necessary financial
allocations I give notice that I intend to make the decision to
extend the contracts as set out above.
 
If you would like to make any representations
to me on this issue please do so by 10
March 2026.

The initial decision
not to extend the contracts for the Purton and Lower Compton HRCs
on the basis of the original offer from Hills Waste was made at a
meeting of Cabinet on 9 December 2025. Following receipt of an
updated and improved offer from Hills Waste which produced a
reasonable financial outcome for the Council, Cabinet resolved to
amend its draft budget proposals at its meeting on 3 February 2026
to allow extension of the contracts by removing the initially
planned budget savings from the closures.
 
As Full Council has
now approved the budget at its meeting on 24 February 2026, an
Executive decision to formally confirm rescission of the decision
made on 9 December 2025 is proposed for procedural reasons, given
the February meeting of Cabinet to retain the sites for at least
the periods listed above already determined the intended course of
action.
 
This approach to
formally confirm the decision is considered to be a proportionate
procedural step to confirm the desired outcome of Cabinet and Full
Council, provides for open administration, and is clear in the
intended outcome and aims. The options and reasons have been set
out above following consideration of professional advice, with the
goal of obtaining best value for the council and communities and to
promote the economic and environmental wellbeing of the county. As
a procedural decision to give effect to prior resolutions of
Cabinet and Council, a Cabinet Member decision is the most
appropriate route to determine the matter in a timely manner.

The Cabinet Member may resolve to:
 
(i) Confirm the
proposed decision
 
(ii) Not confirm the decision
 
As Full Council has already approved a budget
on the basis of the contracts being extended, as recommended by
Cabinet at an earlier meeting, confirming this decision is a
procedural matter to give effect to the earlier resolutions.

Although no formal consultation took place on
altering the initial decision there were a series of public
engagements following the meeting of Cabinet in December 2025,
including meetings of Royal Wootton Bassett & Cricklade Area
Board and Calne Area Board on 20 January 2026 and 5 February 2026
respectively. Engagement with Hills Waste Solutions took place
across this period on potential options.
 
Between those Area Board meetings, it had been
announced that the intention was to reverse the initial decision,
with a budget proposal to finance that change agreed by Cabinet at
its meeting on 3 February 2026.
 
That budget was then approved by Full Council
on 24 February 2026 with all 98 Members in attendance.

purpose:
Wiltshire Council is the statutory
commissioner of a comprehensive integrated sexual health services
including contraception services and sexually transmitted
infections (STI) testing and treatment.



The current contract for the existing service expires on 31 March
2027 and there is now the requirement to commission further service
provision as of 01 April 2027, funded by the Public Health Grant at

term).
content:
Resolved:
 
That Cabinet:
 
1)   
Recognise the requirement to commission a comprehensive sexual
health service that includes free contraceptive services[KB1] , STI testing and treatment,
chlamydia screening and HIV testing and the delivery of HIV
pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP).
 
2)   
Agree to delegate responsibility to tender, commission,
negotiate and award the contract (as appropriate) to the Director
of Public Health and in consultation with the Cabinet Member for
Public Health and Co-ordination with the NHS.
 
Reason for Decisions

 
The commissioning
of sexual health and contraceptive health services is a statutory
public health function under the Health and Social Care Act (2012)
and is a prescribed function of the public health grant which is
under the responsibility of the Director of Public Health. The
current contract expires on 31 March 2027, there is a need to procure this service to
ensure no gap in delivery of services.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to commission a comprehensive sexual health service including free contraceptive services and STI testing, delegating responsibility to the Director of Public Health.

purpose:
To seek approval for procurement of
Electricity and Gas Purchasing Contract.
Current contract expires 31st March 2027. New contract needs to be
awarded by June 2026 to allow for forward buying and
transition.
content:
Resolved:
 

1)   
That cabinet approve the recommended procurement strategy, that
being to award a contract through a Public Sector Framework as the
method by which we purchase electricity and gas supplies from
1st April 2027 for a period of up to 5 years.

 

2)   
That cabinet delegate authority to the Director Assets, in
consultation with the Deputy Leader & Cabinet Member for
Communities, Partnerships, Engagement, Libraries, Leisure, Culture,
Corporate Services, Governance, & Operational Services, to
proceed with the award through a Public Sector Framework from 1st
April 2027 for the initial 3-year term.

 

3)   
That cabinet delegate authority to the Director Assets, in
consultation with the Deputy Leader & Cabinet Member for
Communities, Partnerships, Engagement, Libraries, Leisure, Culture,
Corporate Services, Governance, & Operational Services, to
utilise and award the 2-year extension option, subject to adequate
supplier performance and mutual agreement by both parties.
 
Reason for Decisions

 
The current energy
purchasing arrangement expires on 31st March 2027 and
needs to be replaced to enable the council to continue to deliver
cost-effective electricity and gas supplies to the corporate,
housing, streetlighting and school portfolios. 
 
The strategy for
purchasing energy has changed and developed over the previous
iterations of this contract and has evolved from a fixed price
model to a more flexible strategy that allows the council to cap
budgets and return any savings achieved from lower prices directly
back to the council. 
 
The council’s
Energy Team and Procurement Team have assessed the market and the
service providers regularly over the last 15 years and each time
have concluded that a Public Sector Framework offers the most
suitable service for local authority energy purchasing. Up to 80%
of Local Authorities in the UK utilise these frameworks. They
provide good value for money with the cost of the raw energy being
very competitive as well as providing additional services such as
billing validation, siteworks assistance, query management and
direct access to billing through a web portal.
 
These services
enable the energy team to proactively manage energy on behalf of
the council without the burden of liaison with energy suppliers and
with minimal administration burdens.
